title: Upcoming aligners Symposium to explore digital workflows and biomechanics
html:
Dental Tribune International

Thu. 12. November 2026

share save

Advances in digital workflows, materials and biomechanics are expanding the possibilities of clear aligner therapy, particularly in treatment planning and the management of complex cases. These developments will be explored at the aligners Symposium 2026, a free online continuing education event taking place on 20 November on the DT Study Club platform. Seven expert-led sessions will offer clinical insights for orthodontists and general dentists seeking to expand their treatment options.

Two sessions will examine the material science, biomechanics and clinical applications of Graphy’s Shape Memory Aligners. In the first, Dr Björn Ludwig, an orthodontist and academic affiliated with Saarland University in Germany, will explore the clinical potential of directly 3D-printed aligners, including their integration into digital workflows and the challenges associated with their use. In the second session, Dr Ravindra Nanda, professor emeritus of orthodontics at the University of Connecticut in the US, will further examine shape-memory aligner technology, including material properties, biomechanics and clinical applications. Together, the presentations will address treatment planning, force delivery, thermal activation and current limitations, drawing on research findings and clinical cases.

Beyond her orthodontic practice, Dr Melissa Shotell advocates for women in leadership roles within dentistry and provides professional education on aligner treatment, including online courses on in-office aligner fabrication and hands-on training. (Image: Dr Melissa Shotell)

Dr Melissa Shotell, a board-certified orthodontist based in California in the US, will focus on complex aligner cases, particularly in adult patients requiring restorative care. Drawing on her professional experience, Dr Shotell will guide participants through the selection of appropriate aligner systems, considering their design, materials and mechanics, and the integration of digital tools and workflows, including intra-oral scanning, CBCT, digital treatment planning and remote monitoring.

Regarding the role of digital treatment planning in interdisciplinary treatment, Dr Shotell told Dental Tribune International: “Digital treatment planning can improve clinical outcomes for adult patients by creating a comprehensive plan for the final orthodontic tooth position and final restorative treatment plan.” The webinar will also cover strategies to enhance patient communication. In this regard, Dr Shotell highlighted the value of digital visualisation in helping patients understand the planned aesthetic outcomes of combined orthodontic and restorative treatment, supporting treatment acceptance.

Additional sessions will cover the integration of tooth whitening into aligner treatment, the use of 4D aligners to support clinical and practice efficiency, digital approaches to comprehensive dental treatment and strategies for accelerating orthodontic treatment.

The symposium forms part of the DT Study Club specialty symposium series, which has attracted several thousand dental professionals worldwide since its launch in 2025. Participation is free of charge, although advance registration is required. Dental professionals can earn up to five continuing education credits by watching the webinars and successfully completing the corresponding quizzes.. Registration is open on the DT Study Club website.
